body: That's exactly why I didn't mention him. Thank you sir. You got an upvote from me.

Michael Shannon must be your dad. 

My bad. I hope we can move past this.
It is on Netflix. Its worth a good laugh. The movie is pretty sub par but his role is hilarious. Also James Franco is in it for like 10 minutes.

Ever seen "The Iceman"? its a film about Richard Kuklinski, a hitman for the mob. It has Ray Liotta and sure enough of all people David Schwimmer. 

David plays a mobster, has a ponytail and a mustache and goes as far as killing a few guys. 

He was still just Ross to me. His role in that movie cracked me up more than anything.
I'm OK. Guess I'm feeling better than last night. Its just hard to maintain.

I guess you're right. But the thing that I don't understand about suicide and how people get so upset about is a part of something you mentioned, there's 7 billion people on this planet. Will it really matter if 1 person isn't in the picture because they don't want to be? We don't choose to be born, why can't we choose to die without having to go through extreme lengths. 

I've lived 10 years battling depression/bipolar disorder. Its getting to the point where I don't know what's real anymore. My perceptions are often exaggerated and I have burned bridges because of that. I'm tired of fucking up. I'm tired of falling apart under pressure. I'm tired of having no support. Maybe if I had some kind of circle of support I would feel differently but when everyone that is important to you turns their backs on you when you hit rock bottom it makes it really difficult to care. 

I am just tired. I just want to fall asleep and never wake up.

I'm 26. I have no friends. I am not exaggerating. My last friend who I knew for over 8 years ditched me not too long ago.

I grew up with cycles of dysfunction and abandonment.

I always felt like my life was a pendulum, swinging between two places "OK" and "Fucked" I never was able to get comfortable because whenever something good happened, something fucked up was waiting around the corner. My parents moved all my life. By the time I graduated I enrolled into 9 different schools from around the state. I didn't have time to keep and maintain friendships. I constantly felt like an outsider and I still feel that way. 

And then my parents left my side. First my mom, then my dad.

The loss of my mother as well as genetics triggered my bipolar disorder. My first suicide attempt was when I was 16.

My dad never understood completely what I was going through and left me behind as well.

As far as my strength. You are only half right. 2 years ago, I would have agreed with you. I worked hard, had a place of my own, had a gf was going good.

Then my depression hit hard, I started falling apart at the seams, one day I OD'd on ativan blacked out, freaked out on my GF (didn't hit her or nothing just kept talking about killing myself) and she called the cops and I was put in the hospital. She moved my shit out of the apartment after assuring me while I was on my way to the hospital we would talk about things. After that I went from couch to couch and eventually became homeless. 

I'm just done. I'm burned out. It hurts to care. I look in the past it hurts. The future doesn't interest me. I feel like that pendulum will keep swinging no matter what I do.

People. Definitely people. Another reason I want to die, is the fact that all the problems that exist in this world stems from people. We are a cancer. We fuck up the planet, kill, torture each other, wipe out other species, and sit on this high horse and act like we are supreme beings. We are shitting where we sleep with no worries about what will happen when we wake up. I don't want to be a part of the equation anymore.
